title: The Glory of Martyrs vs. the Ignorance of Tyrants
english: Marketplaces and stalls were set up in the bodies of those who praised, not only men but also women, the most wretched of all. Others were burned by fire, others were struck down by cold; in various ways they shared their excellence among us, so that by falling, they might conquer.

Because of this, having surrounded the pious bodies with reverence—the vessels of election, the instruments of blessed souls, the dwellings of the philosophers—we guard them as highly precious heirlooms for all time, and we protect them as our own treasure; and for the martyrs, the church is fortified like a city with brave soldiers, and all kinds of festivals are celebrated, and we enjoy the joy of the feasts.

But those pressed by hardship or misfortune, as if seeking refuge, rush to the thrice-blessed, making themselves ambassadors of their prayers and requests with great boldness. From here, poverty is relieved, diseases are healed, and the threats of rulers are calmed; and for all the troubles and hardships of life, the shrines of the martyrs are safe harbors.

Thus a father or mother, taking up a sick child and embracing it, runs to seek medicine and doctors, but turns to unskilled help; and coming to one of the martyrs, she presents her petition to the Lord with the same cries used toward the Mediator: 'Intercede through Christ's suffering for those who suffer and are sick. With boldness, use your voice for fellow-servants. Even if you left our life behind, you know the sufferings of humanity; you yourself once pleaded before becoming a martyr. When you sought, you received; now having received, grant. Ask for your own benefit in the form of old age. May we be healed of our infirmity as the world is healed by Christ.'

Another, hastening to a marriage, makes the prayer in the martyr-shrines a prelude to the bridal chambers; and someone rushing to a voyage does not first loosen the moorings of the ship, before he invokes the Lord of the sea through the martyrs; and for the poor and the needy, they have gained a common table and food, the rest of the martyrs; and the martyrs are sung of throughout the earth and the sea. Appropriately and according to their worth. For not as many [do] the righteousness [correctly]...

They bore the cross with their own bodies; they did not scatter money, but poured out blood; they did not kill the poor, but did not pity themselves; they did not visit the maltreated in prison, but they themselves wore the chains. Because of this, in exchange for endurance and affliction, they reaped glory and honor.

10.5.1 Thus are the martyrs; but where are those tyrants and murderers, who thought high things and threatened with arrogance, who sit upon lofty thrones and do not know their own ruler? They have leaped over the lions, run over the leopards, fought against the bears, poured out blood against the wolves, and acted wickedly like foxes. More filthy lie the dead donkeys, for oblivion has covered their lives; but they have a tomb that is terrible, a monument of impiety, and a memory of dishonor; they repent in vain, and they groan uselessly.

10.5.2 But the memory of those insulted by them is received by an unceasing remembrance, an ageless praise. For the accounts and the honors, being received by the drunkards from the elders, and grandfathers to grandsons or fathers to children, passing on the healing care for them, make the praise immortal; and just as life preserves these feasts as an inviolable inheritance, or rather something more precious than an inheritance. For indeed, beautiful things of an inheritance are either taken away by a robber, or an enemy takes them as plunder, or a turn of circumstances empties them; but no one shall cut off the feast of holy men from a year, until they are years and time runs and heaven holds the sun and earth grazes its own animals and the sea its exceptional things.

10.5.3 To speak more truly, even when these elements have ceased, though it may seem so to some, the glory of martyrs and righteous ones shall not be extinguished, nor shall that which concerns them be destroyed by the fury of the people; but then they shall blossom even more toward the incorruptible life, once humanity has been re-adorned.

title: The distinction between honoring martyrs and worshipping idols
english: Stories are given to those who honor the struggles. As if someone were a devoted friend of the excellent martyrs, and set his care upon celebrating their sufferings, not a single day of the year would pass unobserved. For the exploits of brave men possess a glory superior to the solar cycle.

Because the one who opposes the good has attacked the Christian faith fiercely, and sought to destroy all through his schemes and calamities, and to occupy himself vainly with the tasks of the flesh, God, having anointed a multitude of excellent men with commands and trained them for endurance and strength, set them against the shameless and the enemy of humanity.. These, moreover, faced a new kind of struggle. For they did not prevail by striking or smashing, but they excelled   by suffering and by being slaughtered.

And what kind of power would you say, listener, is this of war? And what kind of success is this: to be twisted and flogged, and to have one's life destroyed through fire or sword or the cruelty of prisons? But learn how the wars for piety are won in a different way than other wars. For some have excellence in killing, but others achieve victory without bloodshed through suffering and falling. And the boldness of the righteous carries out missions against the world. And the enemy was caught off guard by the adversaries, whether he fell or intended to. For however many he slaughtered as martyrs, so many helpers of men he prepared.

And in every kind of action, this is found in suffering; therefore, where they think they are obstructing piety, they actually prepare its increase. For the wise God stands against the purposes of the fool and the thoughtless. And we find this throughout the events of every time: the exposition of Moses and the conduct of Joseph. Immediately in the beginning, the second man murdered Abel (Gen 4:8), so that he might cut off the seed of the pious, yet it became fruitful. For from then on, man-slayers are intensely hated, which is why Cain was cursed by God (Gen 4:15). The matter of Christ, that the Satan worked in the Jews so that they might crucify him (Matt 27), is the same. The same thing has happened to the martyrs, whom many despise, trivializing their [life/existence] through their own folly...
A reproach. Is he not a man? Was not the body spent? Is not their memory contained in a few remains and these things? Especially Greeks and Euomians say these things; let us speak to both.

We do not worship martyrs, but honor them as genuine worshippers of God; we do not revere men, but marvel at those who, in the time of trials, have reverently served God well. We place them in beautiful shrines and raise up houses of their rest with magnificent constructions, so that we may emulate the honors of those who well finished their course; and we do not show our zeal for them for pay, but we enjoy their protection toward God.

For our prayer is not sufficient to move God in the time of necessity or misfortune, for our plea is not a persuasion, but a remembrance of sins; therefore we fly to the fellow-servants who are loved by the Lord, so that they might heal our defects through their own achievements. What then is the charge, that while honoring martyrs we ourselves strive to please God? What accusation is there in flying to protectors? Let us examine also these things, if the accuser cleanses the charge. And how [can it be said], that you do not honor myriads of dead men, but worship them as gods?

Did you not, through your folly, deify Demeter and Kore, and yet you honor two women with temples and these sacrifices and with all kinds of worships and healings? Are not the mysteries at Eleusis the essence of your religion, and the Attic people and all Greece flowing together to complete a vanity? Is not the dark descent there, and the solemn gatherings of the hierophant toward the altar, only from woman to woman? Do not the torches go out, and the large and countless people think their salvation to be the things done in the darkness by the two?

Do I say that you worship Dionysus the Theban as a god? For I say, know your fatherland, so that you may know the man: a man, a grape-grower and a vintner, a village leader, a people drawing together and acting shamefully through drunkenness, doing those things which incite the dissolute youths to unchastity, while they drink with the old Silenus and the satyrs who love revelry.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The danger of pride and the legacy of the saints
english: Are you sharing in a life of drunkenness and revelry? You are not the one offering sacrifices to the man Heracles as if he were a god, but to a Roman man, a body who was lucky and brave, and you revere him because he excelled in many things and was surrounded by beasts.

And again, why do you not revere and set aside Asclepius, who was in the porch and surrounded by much iron? And you would not deny that you do this. For the temples rising everywhere in the inhabited world—I say the Asclepieia, the Heracleia, and the Dionysia—stand as clear indictments of your vanity. And so I shall depart innocent of the reproach, for I do not worship idols nor consider them gods; but you are growing, being held by reproaches, and accusing others of these things, just as those with a guilty conscience accuse the innocent. For you show yourself to be worshipping men as gods. These things are few among the many regarding the pagans..

But you Jews of the new stance, what is wonderful that you dishonor Christ, rejecting the likeness to the Father, separating them in your own words, while guarding the places as sacred, in which holy bodies have rested? But you, who have not come to an understanding of what is happening, fear, you who are called Christians, and yet hate the martyrs along with the Greeks. Do you not know how Christ, the Arch-martyr, first suffered and left zeal to the servants?

Then after him Stephen, the namesake of the orthodox struggle according to God; all the following disciples and apostles. And you have inspected through a single insult how many you dishonor: John the Baptist, James called the brother of the Lord, Peter, Paul, Thomas; these I name as the leaders of the martyrs, and then the infinite multitude of those who died for life. Is it not a small thing for you to stumble over these? Is the danger of your hatred not small?

Each of these conquered the devil with the company of demons, and was inscribed among the angels and is kept as a well-pleasing athlete by the promise of the resurrection; and he shall stand at the appearance of God and our Savior, opening his mouth with boldness, rejoicing in the sight of the angels and in the glory of God, blessing himself for the lashes, the chains, the tortures, the [deformities]...

It is a profit of the end, because of the eternal life he has become a guest. But when you hear these things, I know what you think and say: 'I too am acceptable to my peers. If I live according to virtue, I shall be no worse or less honored than those now admired.' Truly, such words are the mark of a proud man, following the great Pharisee (Luke 18:11) and stranger to all humility. It is evident that he who has not previously been humbled will not ascend to height; for a decision is a master.

To ensure that no one forgives you for becoming such a person—tell me, do you not wish to feel shame before those who cut the path of piety for you, the guides of the good, the teachers of virtue, who trained you in endurance and contempt for death? You were taught gratitude from the disciples of this life, that becoming like those who taught and lacking nothing of the art, they nonetheless love the hearts of the teachers, respect them, speak well of them, yield to the first ones, and serve them as a father.

Many also, having ended their lives, holy saints are able, even after departing from life, to do good to men; and witness to these things is Elisha, who long ago, having departed from life and fallen asleep, but having received the grace of God immortal and inseparable, was present in the earth and with the lifeless bones (2 Kings 13:21). For you know, as a lover of the Scriptures and a disciple, that someone dead, being carried out by his own people, perhaps being seized by robbers or enemies, such as it is pleasing to happen in commotion and noise, having been thrown upon the tomb of the thrice-blessed prophet, was immediately revived and rose to the living.

What then shall we say regarding what happened? Did the righteous man have no perception of what was being done? Did he not send up a prayer for the dead as for the child of the woman of Samos? But the truth of things gives us nothing of the sort to conceive. For the righteous man lay there long ago, the body having been dissolved into kindred soil and like dust. But it has become evident that God, always glorifying His own people even after their end, performs wondrous paradoxes concerning their tombs and their resting places, so that the living, always having a more intoxicating hold on the good hope, may hold onto those who have departed.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
